client_alerts.headline: Banks moving to fence off third-party AI agents
client_alerts.body: Axios reports that Morgan Stanley, Bank of America and other large banks are racing to contain unvetted third-party AI agents that can reach customer accounts. The hard part is telling a customer's intent apart from an agent going beyond it. **Financial-services clients should add agent-initiated transactions to their BIA and incident playbooks now.**

client_alerts.headline: M365 Copilot MC1472007 deadline is tomorrow (Oct 25)
client_alerts.body: The change covers advanced agent and plugin uploads, which **stay open to all users by default** unless admins restrict them. Clients on M365 should confirm their agent-upload policy before Monday.

top_moves.title: "Black October": AI-found PHP flaws trigger a global patch scramble
top_moves.body: CNBC and AIWeekly report that PHP2Shell, a set of critical PHP vulnerabilities that AI models helped researchers find, is drawing millions of attack attempts. It shows the gap between AI-speed discovery and exploitation is now days, not weeks.

top_moves.title: China-linked group used agentic AI to speed up a major supply-chain attack
top_moves.body: Reported Oct 23: attackers used AI agents to compress reconnaissance and staging in a supply-chain compromise. Assume adversary timelines are shorter when you set recovery-time objectives and patch SLAs.

top_moves.title: Big banks race to contain third-party AI agents touching customer accounts
top_moves.body: Axios: Morgan Stanley, Bank of America and peers are building controls for agents acting on customers' behalf. This is the first broad financial-sector move to treat consumer AI agents as a third-party risk category.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: OpenAI is reported close to a bridge round of up to $30B at a $1.25T pre-money valuation, below the $1.4T it pitched earlier this month.
providers.detail: The lower valuation lands as a renewed big-tech sell-off driven by skepticism over AI infrastructure spending hit markets on Oct 23. On the product side, ChatGPT added locked chats (Oct 20), which hide chosen conversations behind a PIN or device authentication. GPT-6.1 Sol remains the Codex default. The funding figures come from newsletter reporting and are unconfirmed.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: No new release after the Duet waitlist (Oct 23); the public S-1 has still not been filed.
providers.detail: Duet, an assistant that acts on connected apps and asks for approval before deleting, paying, signing or sending, is in waitlist preview for US Pro and Max. The IPO remains in confidential SEC review since June, with no public filing or roadshow date found.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: No new release; the consumer tier changes continue to roll through.
providers.detail: Free accounts have been limited to Flash-Lite since Oct 9, and Google AI Plus loses Pro on emailed dates. Gemini 4 Argon (reported Oct 1) is still confirmed by only one changelog aggregator.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Quiet since Grok Voice 3.0 (Oct 14); Grok 5 has a week left to meet the prediction-market Oct 31 line.
providers.detail: Grok 4.7 (Sep 21) remains the flagship and is on Amazon Bedrock. SpaceXAI shipped an experimental TypeScript SDK on Oct 2. No xAI announcement confirms Grok 5 timing.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: No new release; Muse Spark replaced Llama in April and Meta's frontier work remains closed.
providers.detail: No open-weight Llama release found. The codenamed Avocado successor is expected to be proprietary.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: No new release; the Large 4 preview (Oct 6) is still API-only, with open weights promised.
providers.detail: A user roundup mentions a 'Le Chonk 1T' model with open weights coming, but it is unconfirmed by Mistral.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: No dated October product release found; publisher lawsuits (at least seven) remain the story.
providers.detail: Model Council and Perplexity Computer remain the paid-tier differentiators. Nothing new in the window.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: MC1472007 takes effect tomorrow (Oct 25): advanced agent and plugin uploads stay open to all users by default.
providers.detail: October also brings a new Copilot home screen, side-by-side Office file editing, and the Copilot prompt box in Word/Excel/PowerPoint (MC1470885, rolling Sep–Dec). Local inferencing and expanded Teams/Entra ID backup are on the roadmap. Separately, Microsoft reported a diagnostic system that beat general physicians on hard cases.
providers.alertReason: Agent/plugin upload default open to all users; deadline Oct 25

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: One unconfirmed report says Computer Use reached public preview in Copilot CLI and the desktop apps.
providers.detail: Only a single Italian outlet reports it; no GitHub changelog confirmation found. Usage-based billing (since June 1) and share loss to Cursor and Claude Code remain the backdrop.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: One unconfirmed report puts Cursor at 3.24 with new safety controls for auto-review.
providers.detail: Same single source as the GitHub item; no Cursor changelog confirmation found.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: No release found; the long quiet stretch continues.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new release; Notion Workers billing against Notion credits started Oct 15.

Anthropic — IPO with no public S-1 — 2+ weeks running (confidential filing since June)
Google Gemini — consumer tier downgrades — 2+ weeks running (Free on Flash-Lite since Oct 9)

month_themes.then: Cheaper frontier quality (Opus 5.5), tiered flagship lineups (GPT-6 Sol/Luna), delayed launches finally landing (Grok 4.7)
month_themes.now: Agentic AI as an attack accelerant, financial-sector controls on consumer agents, and repricing of AI funding amid capex skepticism

habits.shift: Add an 'AI-speed exploitation' scenario (PHP2Shell pattern) to ransomware and patch-failure runbooks; shorten assumed detection-to-exploit windows.
No change; map third-party AI agents to ISO 22301 supplier controls and NIST AI RMF when summarising for clients.
Verify single-source changelog claims (Copilot Computer Use, Cursor 3.24) against vendor pages before citing them.
Offer an 'AI agent third-party risk' assessment add-on, especially to financial-services clients, following the bank moves.
No change; ChatGPT Slides (Oct 16) is worth a trial for shared team decks.

habits.task: Client advisory on AI data risk
habits.shift: Push M365 clients to review MC1472007 agent-upload settings before Oct 25, and brief on approval gates for action-taking assistants like Duet.

community.signal: 'GLM-5.2 is a win for Local AI' is among the most-discussed recent topics (79 related posts per GummySearch).
community.so_what: Open-weight options remain viable for clients who need on-prem inference for data-residency reasons.

community.signal: Ongoing discussion of the US government order to disable certain Anthropic models.
community.so_what: Model availability can change by regulatory order; keep a fallback provider in AI-dependent continuity plans.

community.signal: Recent trending topics include a low-skilled attacker using Claude Code and Codex.
community.so_what: Reinforces today's theme: AI lowers the skill bar for attackers, so tabletop exercises should assume more capable adversaries.
